code.originalText: Two-week follow-up and otolaryngology consultation with same-day audiologic evaluation

text.paragraph: Two-week follow-up, seen the same day by otolaryngology after a full audiologic evaluation. [S]

Mr. van Beethoven returns two weeks after his first visit, on the day of his otolaryngology consultation with Dr. Albrecht and his audiologic evaluation. His hearing feels the same: he still misses soft speech and high notes at a distance, the left ear worse, and loud sounds are painful. The ringing and buzzing are constant in both ears and keep him awake until he plays quiet music. He has had no sudden change in hearing, dizziness, ear pain, discharge, or facial weakness. He has his first therapy session later this week. He has told no one at work. He read his blood results by portal and asked what they meant. [S]

tr.td: Canals clear; eardrums intact and mobile on pneumatic otoscopy
Weber lateralizes to the right; Rinne positive on both sides (air louder than bone)
Cranial nerves II to XII normal, including facial movement and facial sensation; no nystagmus; Romberg negative
Engaged; mood low; no signs of psychosis

Progressive hearing loss in both ears over about three years, worse on the left, with poor understanding of soft speech; type and cause not yet established at intake; audiology and otolaryngology evaluation requested
S — Synthetic presenting concern anchored to his documented account; superseded by the diagnosis at the audiologic evaluation.

Persistent, bothersome tinnitus in both ears for about three years, constant ringing and buzzing day and night, with intolerance of loud sound; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented tinnitus
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented tinnitus.
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood in response to progressive hearing loss, with withdrawal from social gatherings; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented despair and isolation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the documented letters describe distress and withdrawal, and the record makes no claim about his real mental health.

Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, asymmetric (left worse than right), sloping from normal or mild in the low frequencies to moderately severe in the high frequencies; no air-bone gap; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented progressive deafness, whose cause remains unknown
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the audiologic evaluation; it states no cause, because the retrospective theories are disputed.

list.item:
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, asymmetric (H90.3). The presenting hearing loss is now characterized. Audiogram today: sloping sensorineural loss with no air-bone gap; right ear 15 to 25 dB HL through 1000 Hz falling to 60 dB HL at 8000 Hz (four-frequency average 35 dB HL, mild); left ear 20 to 40 dB HL through 1000 Hz falling to 75 dB HL at 8000 Hz (average 49 dB HL, moderate). The left ear is 15 dB worse at 1000, 1775, 3000, and 4000 Hz. Word recognition 88% on the right and 64% on the left; tympanograms normal; acoustic reflexes present at reduced sensation levels, consistent with a cochlear loss; otoacoustic emissions absent above 1500 Hz. Treatable-cause tests were normal: hemoglobin 15.1 g/dL, TSH 1.8 mIU/L, HbA1c 5.2%, treponemal antibody nonreactive (index 0.12). The asymmetry calls for MRI to exclude a vestibular schwannoma or other retrocochlear cause; Dr. Albrecht agrees. [S]
MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium.
Bilateral hearing aids with a music program, a tinnitus sound generator, and a remote microphone, to be fitted by audiology.
Custom musicians' earplugs for loud rehearsals.
Come in the same week for any sudden drop in hearing.

Persistent, bothersome tinnitus, bilateral (H93.13). Bothersome and present for about three years, with hearing loss. Tinnitus Handicap Inventory 58, moderate to severe. Nonpulsatile and not localized to one ear; the MRI is for the hearing asymmetry, not the tinnitus. Medicines and supplements do not help tinnitus and are not recommended. [S]
Education on how tinnitus and hearing loss interact.
Sound enrichment at night.
Cognitive behavioral therapy as planned; hearing aids with sound generators.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21). PHQ-9 11, from 12. Mood Disorder Questionnaire 2, negative, given today because it was missed at intake. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in place. [S]
Begin cognitive behavioral therapy this week.
PHQ-9 at the next visit.
